scene clearnightsky
There is no second half of “My Indigo.”
It’s one of those poems that comes and goes — like sunlight in the afternoon when it finds the gaps between leaves and squeezes through them, spilling itself out onto the asphalt.
I often wonder how I would look splayed out upon the asphalt, but the manner in which I envision that is a lot less aesthetically pleasing.
We’re heading back to the bathhouse, I think. Or some other place that Io wants to go, but she hasn’t said much ever since leaving the restaurant and I don’t think it’s safe to ask her.
It goes without saying, but she reminds me of myself sometimes. Especially when her voice fades out.
So as the moon attempts to mimic the sun and cast its light through the trees, this is what I’m thinking of.
But the differences between Io and me are just as noticeable as that of the sun and the moon.
One of us is stronger, one of us is weaker. But neither one of us can agree on which is which. Which is fine, because it creates just enough space between the two of us that she’ll feel safe.
And so I keep my distance-
But I long to go for a swim.

I’m sure when I was younger, there were times I wanted something I couldn’t have. And given that I still possess the mental maturity of a child at times, I should be okay with this. I should be able to adapt.
I should be okay with keeping my swim trunks locked in the drawer until the setting is right and the sun has no tree to meld with.
But I really want to go for a swim.
And I want to take her with me.
: Sorry for being stupid again. I left my safety net at home.
: The one with Uta or the one with naked people? Because I’m not really sure where we’re headed right now.
: The latter. I haven’t really been staying at the dorm as much as I used to lately.
: Any reason why?
: I just don’t like girls very much.
: Wow, really? I had no idea.
: How do you do it, Sensei? Or...how did you do it before you too learned to appreciate just how great it is to live a life of mostly solitude?
: I’m sure my sexual attraction to them played some sort of role in keeping me sane.
: Does it really make that much of a difference?
: I’m not sure. I’ve never really thought about it.
: I’ve just never spent much time around other guys, I don’t think.
: Even when you were younger?
: All I remember from when I was younger is my childhood friend who, and you might want to brace yourself for this, was also a girl.
: Why would I have to brace myself for such a predictable thing?
: You just get so jealous any time another girl comes up that I figured hearing about such a fated connection might hurt your feelings.
: Is she important to you?
: In a lot of ways, she’s the most important person to me.
: And in others?
scene black
: In other ways, part of me wishes she didn’t exist.
scene komorebi1
We make our way into Io’s room because of course we do. We were always going to come here whether I knew it deep down or not because this is where she’s safest.
Not next to me. Not next to Uta. But in a room surrounded by wooden robots and tools and pills and wires and even more pills and everything else that serves as her safety net.
The air is different this time around — and it’s not just because I’m not waking up in some gaudy bathrobe and faux-fur pajama pants.
Maybe it’s the light — and that stale scent of turpentine— or the fact that I am dangerously conscious for the time being.
Whatever it is, it makes me want to fall asleep and never get up.
I want to collapse in her bed, fall asleep in her arms, then awake and brush her hair out of her face before going home and getting scolded by my daughter.
But this is someone else’s daughter. And yes, that’s true of every girl I crawl into bed with, but you know what I mean.
The idea of something so pure and innocent is antithetical to the evils at play here. So again, I keep my distance.
Again I recite “My Indigo.” But I keep stopping at the line “blackness gathers in the grass” and worry that the grass is here and that I am the blackness.
I’m sure that’s not what Lee had in mind when he wrote this poem. My existence matters not to him, nor anyone else with a brain even half as functional.
But Io’s brain is held together by glue and benzodiazepines, and it isn’t strong enough to protect its container from the blue death.
I really want to go swimming.
: You haven’t been here since you accidentally flashed Uta, have you?
: Not unless the two of you dragged me here after breaking into my house. But that whole night is blurry to me and I don’t think either one of you is strong enough.
scene komorebi2
: We kind of just showed up, freaked out, then got forced out of the house by your psychopath of a niece.
: I’m sure she was just trying to protect me.
scene komorebi3
: So does that give other people permission to capture you and hold you in captivity so long as they’re doing it out of what you’d call “the goodness of their heart?” Asking for a friend.
: My answer to that question hinges entirely on whether or not you have a pair of handcuffs in this room.
: And now I’m even more confused because I can’t tell if you want me to have handcuffs or not and I don’t want to say the wrong thing.
scene komorebi4
: Do you want to keep me here forever?
: I don’t know. It sounds nice and all, but it also might make it really hard to go to the amusement park when you finally decide to take me there.
: Let’s go soon.
scene komorebi5
: Really?!
: Yeah. It’s not like I have anything else going on anymore. And I’ve already been there with Tsuneyo twice since first talking to you about it.
: I’m just going to ignore that last part so I can continue to be excited! Heck yeah! Amusement park!
: Don’t get too excited. The fact that it’s an amusement park won’t change the fact that I will continue to be completely unamusing while inside it.
: Doesn’t matter! I suck too, which just means that we can suck together while participating in slightly less sucky activities!
scene komorebi6
: Works for me, Io.
: Sensei? Where are you going?
: Bed. I’m tired.
scene komorebi7
: But we just got here.
: We did. Which means you’re welcome to join me if you’d like.
: You’re giving me permission to enter my own bed?
: That’s right. I’ve seized control of it. This is my bed now.
scene komorebi8
: You’re allowed to do that?!
: We can do anything we want. That’s what it means to be free.
: Then I hereby seize control of your heart and command that you leave behind however many fake girlfriends you have in favor of either me or Uta! Or both.
: Can I bring Ami along?
scene komorebi9
: Ew, no. I’ll never get to see you if she’s there. She’s too clingy.
: And you’re not?
: Not like that. She’s genuinely creepy. I’m just annoying.
: She’s family, Io. I can’t just abandon her even if you do seize control of my heart.
scene komorebi10
: Then what good does seizing it even do in the first place? Besides, isn’t it sort of arbitrary to keep her close-by just because she’s “family?” That word means literally nothing.
: This is your aunt’s house, isn’t it? If family meant nothing, you’d be back at the dorms right now.
: I’m not here for my aunt. I’m here because this is where all of my stuff is.
: But your stuff wouldn’t be here without your aunt is what I’m saying. Which, by extension, means we never would have met without her.
: And, speaking of which, when am I going to meet her? Because I’ve been coming here for a while now and she’s never even-
scene komorebi11
: She travels a lot.
: Where? She can’t leave the city.
: Around? I don’t know. It’s a big city. And you’d have nothing to gain from meeting her anyway.
: It’s not really about gaining anything, it’s about putting a face to a name.
: You don’t even know her name, though.
: Do you not want me meeting her or something?
scene komorebi12
: Was that not immediately obvious?
: It...was. I just don’t really get why.
: Because I want to keep my life with you separate from my life outside of you.
: That’s not really how having a life with someone works, Io. You can’t just hide things from me forever.

: Sure I can. But that’s fine because it means you can also hide things from me, so we don’t accidentally start mixing traumas and make our relationship all messy and sad like everything else in our lives.
: But what if I want to share something with you?
: Then you can. I just don’t want it to be mandatory.
: I’m not proposing we make it “mandatory.” I’m proposing that-
: If you meet her, you’ll meet her. If you don’t, you won’t. It’s as simple as that.
: It’s not like you’re missing out anything. She’s just some random woman with really bad fashion sense.
scene komorebi13
: She’s more than just “some woman.” She’s the person effectively raising you. And if she isn’t doing anything wrong, it’s messed up to just reduce her to that.
: How is it messed up? It’s not like I’m calling her an evil bitch. I’m just saying she is a human being who exists and that you don’t have a good reason to meet her. Which is true.
: You’re right. That is true. I don’t have to meet her. I’ve gotten along just fine without her and I am perfectly content never coming into contact with a woman whose clothes I wore.
: But, as someone currently reevaluating just what it means to be part of a “family,” I have a problem with you talking about her like that.
: Like what? Again, I said literally nothing bad about her. She’s just there.
scene komorebi14
: Do you have any idea how hard “just being there” is?
: Uhh...not hard? Because it is literally as simple as “just being there.” Which is like, the bare minimum amount of activity required to participate in something.
: Just look at how I’ve acted at essentially every single class gathering that we’ve ever-
: Just being there as a person is way different than just being there as a parent.
: Cool. Except she isn’t a parent. She’s my aunt.
: Is she there for you when you need her? Does she give you a place to live and food to eat? Who’s the one refilling all of your prescriptions? Who is giving you money?
: She is, but-
: Then she’s a parent. She’s your mother.
scene komorebi15
: Excuse me?
: Maybe I was wrong when I asked you if you knew how hard it was to “just be there.” What I should have asked is if you know how easy it is to fuck that up.

: You have a problem with Ami, right? Well, the reason she’s like that is because of me. It’s because I wasn’t there that she’s all fucked up now. So if you’re going to blame anyone, blame me for that. Not her.
: What’s going on with you? Why are you getting so beaten up over this? Are you just trying to start a fight with me or something?
: What’s going on is that I think you’re taking your aunt for granted and that isn’t fair to her. She doesn’t have to look after you, but she does. And she gives you everything you need, doesn’t she?
: I could look after myself if I had to. That’s basically what I do anyway.
: Well, that’s good for you. But not everyone can do that. And if Ami had someone like her instead of someone like me, maybe fewer people would hate her for what she’s become.
: Oh, so it’s a personal thing. You’re coming after me because you regret things you have done. Got it. That’s fine. I’ll be a scapegoat if it makes you feel better, Sensei.
: I’m not trying to come after you, Io. I just-
scene komorebi16
: You just want to tell me how I’m supposed to look at family because you’re pretending to be more than just Ami’s uncle now, right? And you want to feel better about the job you’re doing!
: Right?!
: You’re not entirely off-base, but you’re not entirely correct either.
: Well I think it’s cute that you want to play dress-up, Sensei! But maybe you should pretend to be something other than a parent because parents fucking suck and you don’t want to be one!
: You’re right. I don’t want to be one. I have to be one or Ami is going to-

: There’s no fixing that girl, Sensei. Just like there’s no fixing me! And I already have an extended relative who inherited a role that, based on my experience, gets way more credit than it should for literally nothing!
scene komorebi14
: I’ll never get this fascination people have with family. Like, oh! Congrats on having similar DNA structure to someone else! You guys must really love each other!
: That’s not-
: Shut up! I’m not finished! I need to tell you how fucking stupid this topic is so we can go back to liking each other!
: Io-
: I said shut up!
scene komorebi17
: I don’t give a single FUCK about what you want to be or what you think you are, just keep me out of it!
: I don’t NEED family and I don’t NEED to be reminded of how EASY IT IS to fuck up just EXISTING, okay?!
: Parents have ONE FUCKING JOB and it’s to BE THERE. It isn’t hard! It’s really not! And I don’t CARE that I’ve never experienced what it’s like on their end because I don’t HAVE to!
: And here YOU are, playing a game of charades where you get to act out the role of a FATHER for the first time in your life, and you want ME to be thankful for SOMEONE ELSE playing too?!
: Are you an IDIOT? Are you STUPID?! Or do you just HATE kids and get joy out of inflicting pain on them?! Is THAT why you’re doing this?! Is that your end goal here?! Are you one of THEM now?!
: Of course not...
: Then WHY?! Why would you press me about this?! Why would you call my AUNT such a TERRIBLE thing to my face?!
: You DID hear, didn’t you?! YOU HEARD WHAT THEY SAID ABOUT ME! That I’m ROTTEN! SPENT! TRASH!
scene komorebi18
: And you know it’s true...
: But you have no idea what it’s like.
: You’ve never felt like a prisoner...even when you were one.
: You’ve never seen your home as a jail cell. Never had your cries for help ignored by everyone around you.
: Never had to make up stories and excuses about why you’d have panic attacks in the middle of school! And why they weren’t anything for someone to be concerned about! But they were!
: Someone should have done something! SOMEONE SHOULD HAVE HELPED ME! But they didn’t! No one did! Not until the damage had already been done!
: Are THOSE the people you want me to feel sorry for?! The ones who let a little girl ROT and BREAK because THEY had kids of their own?! Or the ones who BROKE ME in the first place?!
: I have no parents. Not anymore.
: I have an aunt and that’s it.
: And if you want me to start seeing her as anything else, you should grab me a bucket because I can’t even say the word “Mom” without wanting to throw up.
scene komorebi19
: Do you want to know how old I was?
: Are you just lying to me now?
: Then what were you doing with that picture of Uta?
scene komorebi20
: What...picture of Uta?...
: You know exactly what I’m talking about...
: It wasn’t just a misunderstanding...that was all typical wishful thinking from typical Io...

: I mean...what’s there to even misunderstand? You’re just another sick adult who can’t control himself around little girls. And I’m so fucked up by now that it barely even bothers me anymore when it comes to me.
: But Uta...
: Those pictures ruined her life.
: And you’re keeping one as a...fucking trophy.
: How...did you even...
: It doesn’t matter...Nothing matters...I’m done...
: Done with what, Io?...
: Everything.
: Do whatever you want to me. I won’t fight back.
scene komorebi21
: Did you hear that, Aki-kun? She says she won’t fight back. Sounds like consent to me.
: My Indigo...
scene komorebi22
: Hm?
: I've come to find the flower which blossoms...like a saint dying upside down...
scene komorebi23
: The rose won't do, nor the iris. I've come to find the moody one, the shy one, downcast, grave, and isolated...
scene komorebi24
: Right?
: It could be good for her, you know.
: It could be good for you too.
: Maybe she’ll become the next whatshername?
: You’re like me when it comes to this stuff, Aki-kun. And we both know you’ve always looked up to me.
: I won’t tell you what to do — just that you should follow your heart instead of someone else’s.
: And if you think that making love to this girl will do her more good than it will harm, I say do it.
: You’ve always been a special boy. You can fix anything you want so long as you put your mind to it.
: This little one is no exception.
: But you have to make the decision, Aki-kun.
: It has to be you this time.
